notes: Re-coded 2026-10-27 to the multi-option format in issues.json: each position has `options` (one id; two only when words and votes differ; [] when no sourced position is specific enough). Record-based rules used for every incumbent alike: H.R. 1 (roll 190) Yea = medicaid 'keep', Nay = 'reverse'; H.R. 1834 (roll 11) Yea = aca 'restore', Nay plus Yea on H.R. 6703 (no extension) = 'lapse'; H.R. 8 (2021 roll 75) and H.R. 2377 extreme-risk orders (2022 roll 255) both Yea = guns 'checks-red-flag', both Nay = 'enforce'; H.R. 2056 (2025 roll 171, bars D.C. from limiting ICE detainer cooperation) Yea = immigration 'full-help'; WHPA Yea = abortion 'protect'. WHPA Nay alone does not pick among states/earlier-limit/ban; H.J.Res. 72 (Canada only) does not pick a tariff option; SAVE America (roll 69) and H.R. 7008 (roll 280) are bundled and set no voter-id or term-limits option. Roll-call XML was read directly from clerk.house.gov/evs on 2026-10-27.
Issues covered are the F and B items only: voter-id, abortion, guns, immigration, tariffs, aca, medicaid-cuts, term-limits. No race is uncontested; each has at least a Democrat and a Republican.

PA-16: search snippets of Ballotpedia and theballotbrief.com list independent Nick Singelis, but The Green Papers, Spotlight PA, WHYY and Gettysburg Connection list only Kelly and Wagner. Treat him as unverified until the PA Dept of State ballot is checked; drop him if he isn't on it.

Ballotpedia district pages and the PA Dept of State site couldn't be read by my tools (Ballotpedia returned empty pages, so I could not confirm the Singelis listing on it; curl to Ballotpedia was blocked as bot-check circumvention). The ballotSource fields use The Green Papers and Spotlight PA (2026-09-28).

Bill vehicles: H.R. 1834 ('Breaking the Gridlock Act', roll 11, 2026-01-08, passed 230-196) carried the 3-year ACA extension forced by the discharge petition. S.1383 House amendment (roll 69, 2026-02-11, passed 218-213) is the SAVE America Act (proof of citizenship plus photo ID). H.R. 7008 (roll 280, 2026-07-22, passed 232-198) combined the stock-purchase restriction with the Voter ID Act, so it is a bundled vote and is not used alone for either issue. H.J.Res. 72 (roll 65, 2026-02-11, passed 219-211) would end the Canada tariff emergency.
WVIA (2026-02-14) independently confirms that all PA Republicans except Fitzpatrick, Bresnahan and Mackenzie voted no on the ACA extension.
Joyce's 2021 Second Amendment release and Hyde release could not be opened (house.gov returned 403). Their content comes from search snippets; the Hyde release date is unconfirmed.
Thompson's 'fully supportive of Trump' trade quote comes from a search snippet of iowacapitaldispatch.com (403 on fetch). Verify it before publishing, or fall back to his record (Nay on H.J.Res. 72).
Deluzio's guns stance rests on Giffords' characterization, not his own words. His abortion stance comes from his 2022 campaign site as quoted by OnTheIssues.

Capital-Star's questionnaires got no reply from Guy, Bradstock, Wagner, Farnham, Joyce or Reschenthaler. Vote411 and Ballotpedia Candidate Connection could not be read. Both are worth a manual check, especially for Guy and Bradstock, who have the most unknowns.
Gaps left by the search cap: Kelly, Thompson and Reschenthaler's own words on abortion, guns, immigration, voter ID and stock trading; Deluzio's own words on H.R. 7008; Singelis's ballot status.
